small_guidance:
- The kernel does the conv-transpose as a gather but the inner reduction over `IC=16` is tiny — collapse the `ic_start` loop entirely by setting `BLOCK_IC=16` (==IC) and removing the inner Python loop; this lets `tl.dot` see a full K=16 tile each pass with no overhead. Also try larger BLOCK_SPATIAL configs (256, 512) at num_warps=8 since OUT_SPATIAL = 32·64·64 = 131072 is huge.
- Hoist the `valid` mask and `in_spatial` computation outside the IC loop (they don't depend on ic). Better: skip the entire (kd,kh,kw) iteration when SD/SH/SW>1 by iterating only over valid taps for each output coordinate — but since stride=2, ~7/8 of (kd,kh,kw,output) combinations are invalid, so the current code wastes most of its tl.dot work on zeroed inputs. Restructure so the kernel iterates over (kd,kh,kw) but checks `valid` before the IC reduction and skips via masking that zeros the input load (already done) — at minimum gate the `tl.dot` cost by reducing KD*KH*KW=27 loop iterations using the fact that for stride=2 only ~1/8 of taps contribute per output.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_OC=32, BLOCK_SPATIAL=256, BLOCK_IC=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=3 and BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SPATIAL=128, BLOCK_IC=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=3 — verify SMEM: (64·16 + 16·128)·4·3 ≈ 36KB, safe.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM with one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile), but flatten the (kd,kh,kw) loop into the K dimension of the GEMM so K = IC*KD*KH*KW = 16*27 = 432; the GEMM tile then naturally amortizes the index math. The current 3-nested kd/kh/kw loop with a separate tl.dot per tap is leaving the tensor cores underfed — fuse all taps into one K-reduction.
- For stride-2 ConvTranspose3d the gather form has 7/8 wasted taps per output position. Switch to **scatter-add**: one program per (N, IC-tile, input-spatial-tile) computes the input × weight outer product and scatter-adds into the OD×OH×OW output grid. This eliminates the validity-mask waste entirely. Pair with a separate fused epilogue kernel that applies scale/shift and computes the per-(N,OC) spatial mean in one pass (block reduction), then a second kernel (or fused tail) subtracts the mean. The current two-pass (compute+atomic-sum then sub-mean) is fine but the conv stage is the bottleneck.
- Use channels_last (NDHWC) layout for input/output so the IC and OC axes are contiguous; this makes the GEMM-K loads coalesced and avoids the strided ID*IH*IW gather stride currently in `x_off`. Materialize the transposed weight once at init in (KD,KH,KW,OC,IC) order to match.
